text: Write the opening of a story called Hide! The story is about a character who witnesses something
that puts them in danger. In your writing, create a sense of drama and suspense.
Write two contrasting diary entries (300–450 words each), the first by a young woman wondering
what her life will be like when she is older, and the second by the same woman when she is in
her 80s, looking back on her life when she was younger. In your writing, create a sense of the
woman’s outlook and mood.
Write a descriptive piece called Flying. In your writing, create a sense of atmosphere, and focus
on colours, sounds and movements to help your reader imagine the scene.
Section B: Writing for an audience
A new sports magazine aimed at teenagers and young adults has recently been launched. Write a
review of the magazine, which will be published in your school newsletter.
Your school recently arranged a trip to a museum. Your head teacher has asked for formal
feedback on the trip. Write two contrasting letters to the head teacher (300–450 words each), one
from a student who gained from the experience, and another from a different student who found
the experience less useful.
Write the script of a voiceover for the opening segment of a TV documentary called Goodbye
Boredom! The programme is aimed at teenagers, and focuses on how to make the most of free
time. In your writing, offer advice and guidance, and create a sense of fun and enthusiasm.
